rows.name: placement?
rows.notes: Left undefined on purpose. A root menu falls back to `bottom-start` and a submenu to `right-start`, and which of the two applies is only known once the parent has been wired — so the resolution is a `computed`, not a default.

rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: closeOnSelect?
rows.notes: Overridable per item through `getItemProps({ closeOnSelect })`.

rows.name: preventOutsideActivation?
rows.notes: The native behaviour, and the one the reference app's own context menu had (parity M5): the click that closes a menu must not also activate whatever was under it.

rows.name: modal?
rows.notes: `false`, and that is a decision rather than an omission. `layer-stack` documents `modal` as "inert plus scroll lock" — the dialog's contract, and disproportionate for a menu. Confinement comes from the dismissable layer and the intent stack instead.

rows.name: preventScroll?
rows.notes: Defaults to the `sheet` presentation and is ignored in `popup`.

rows.name: selectionFlash?
rows.notes: The selection blink. Off in `sheet` and under reduced motion, whatever is asked.

rows.name: label?
rows.notes: The accessible name when the surface has no trigger to be labelled by.

rows.name: trigger?
rows.notes: Handed to `MenuTrigger` as `render` — never as its children. The trigger *is* a `<button>`, and a button inside a button is `nested-interactive`. Exactly one of `trigger` and `contextTrigger`; the function's own signature refuses both at once.

rows.name: contextTrigger?
rows.notes: The region a right click, a long press, Shift+F10, the ≣ key or the pad's `contextMenu` intent opens the surface from. Children rather than `render`, because `MenuContextTrigger` is a plain container with no handler of its own — the listeners are installed natively by the machine, since they have to be listening while the surface is closed. A surface with neither anchor is legal and is the store-driven shape: `open` on one side, `label` for the name the trigger would have given it.

rows.name: cancelLabel?
rows.notes: The action sheet's Cancel row, handed straight to `MenuContent`, which renders it in the `sheet` presentation and nowhere else. The library ships no copy of its own; `null` is read as absent for the reason the part reads `undefined` that way — `getCancelTriggerProps` writes no accessible name, so an empty button would be a nameless one.

rows.name: container?
rows.notes: Reaches every portal in the tree, so a submenu cannot escape its parent's host.

rows.name: keepMounted?
rows.notes: Keeps every surface in the tree mounted while closed; the sheet hides them.

rows.name: renderItem?
rows.notes: Replaces the CHILDREN of a row, never the row. `defaults` is what the layer would have rendered — the checkmark cell on a checkable, the symbol, the text, the subtitle, the shortcut — and it is handed over so that **decorating** is the cheapest thing to do, not because replacing is impossible. Rendering something else instead of `defaults` is the consumer's to do and costs them the part that names the row (`MenuItemText`), the checkmark, and the leading column those two share. Decorate as a **sibling** of `defaults`, never by wrapping it in an element: a row's children are its grid cells (`_menu.scss`, `grid-template-columns` on `menu:item`), each one placed by `grid-column`, so a wrapper takes all of them out of the grid at once. Rows only. A group is not one, a separator is not one, and a submenu's trigger item is not one either — it opens a surface rather than choosing, and the sheet draws its chevron as a pseudo-element on the row itself.

name: MenuEntry
definition: MenuRow<V, Meta> | MenuSubmenu<V, Meta> | ComposedGroup<MenuEntry<V, Meta>> | ComposedSeparator

rows.name: portal?
rows.notes: Reaches every surface in the tree, the root's and each submenu's.

rows.name: itemGroup?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY group — `id` and `label` are the entry's, one per group.

rows.name: item?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY row, hence no `id` **and no IDREF**: one id repeated down a menu is a broken reference per row, and one `aria-labelledby` repeated gives every row the same name — which no dangling-IDREF check can see, because the id it points at does resolve. `ref` goes for the same reason: a single ref held by N rows ends up holding the last one.

rows.name: triggerItem?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY submenu row, and repeated for the same reasons.

rows.name: id?
rows.notes: The nested machine's scope id, and the one field a group's `id` and this one do not share a reason for. A group needs it or its `aria-labelledby` dangles; a submenu without it is correct — `useMachine` mints one from React's own id hook, and the server and the client agree on it. What it buys is what a group's key buys: every id under this surface becomes the consumer's rather than React's, which is what a server render has to match to the character.

name: MenuAction
definition: Omit< CoreMenuItemProps, "value" | "label" | "description" > & ComposedDecoration<Meta> & { readonly value: V; readonly label: string; readonly description?: string | undefined; }

name: MenuCheckable
definition: Omit< CoreMenuOptionItemProps, "value" | "label" | "description" > & ComposedDecoration<Meta> & { readonly value: V; readonly label: string; readonly description?: string | undefined; }

rows.name: cancelLabel?
rows.notes: The action sheet's Cancel button, rendered for you (components.md §3-1): pass the word and the part appears in the `sheet` presentation and nowhere else. Left out, nothing is added — the library ships no copy of its own, and a nameless button is worse than none (the machine warns about one in dev).

rows.name: id
rows.notes: Ties the group to its label. Any stable string the consumer owns.

rows.name: label?
rows.notes: The group renders an `itemGroupLabel` part — wires `aria-labelledby`. Same shape as `MenuItemProps.description` and declared for the same reason: `connect` is pure, so it cannot look for the label. Written unconditionally the attribute is worse than absent — the group ends with no accessible name *and* a dangling IDREF, which axe reports as `incomplete` rather than a violation, so no test catches it.
